text_parts.literal: The scoped mathematical conclusions are Theorems 1–3 in `argument.md` and `P05.1-paper.tex`. Their full proof coverage is 299 L0–L5, 296 C1–C5, and 297 B1–B3. The three working files are unreviewed inputs, not accepted dependencies. The proposed units survive the independent reconstruction, with two explicit precision points: point faces have zero intrinsic Lipschitz constant but may require nonzero ambient support bounds; exact rational contacts belong to unshifted majorants, not to the decreasing shifted sequence.

The main theorem requires a finite pure-dimensional globally embedded rational complex, all boundary faces present, strictly positive actual real balanced top weights, a fixed rational refinement carrying the actual continuous real PA affine reference, and a continuous printed-PC function with a two-sided uniform bound. Its conclusion is global Euclidean Lipschitzness on each convex closed cell, and bounded ambient supports on entire incident cells at every face point. Polygonal paths inherit the bound. Unrestricted ambient-distance Lipschitzness across nonincident cells/components is not claimed. No PC or positive-growth assumption on gamma is needed for this theorem; no quotient-normal independence or complete-plane condition is used.

The single-cell theorem needs global Lipschitzness in addition to convexity and bounded affine difference. The orthant example proves this extra input cannot be omitted. The auxiliary Gamma is a proper convex real PA function on one whole affine hull with rational walls and exact agreement with the actual affine restriction on its whole cell. It is not a substituted global reference. The norm-infimum extension and its maximum with Gamma-C are finite convex continuous functions and can be non-PA. They receive no measure. Actual real majorants use rational spatial samples with actual real heights, not rationalized function values or a rationalized dual polytope.

Finite rational contacts are exact in the unshifted construction and can be appended arbitrarily finitely. They cannot constrain an arbitrary trace on a whole positive-dimensional overlap. Chord majorants of t² on [0,1] give concrete different convex rational-carrier traces which agree at a prescribed finite rational contact set and have arbitrarily small uniform error. Distinct incident-cell approximants also have no proved common ambient supporting functional. The direction-cost PCC argument is proved for the original function, not for independent choices of its approximants.

Consequently, no joint uniform PA regularization theorem is established on arbitrary finite balanced complexes with several positive-dimensional overlaps. No further compatible-extension lemma is claimed. For R230's actual all-C_b envelope, the scoped theorem gives Lipschitzness and per-cell majorants, but a genuine compatible global approximation domain must be proved before a completed mixed operator can be applied. Upper-only and bounded competitor equality is proved in the PC domain by a continuous PC maximum; it is not arbitrary maximum closure in the rational-carrier scalar real PA domain.

All frozen qualified scopes remain: finite-global noncompact exclusions do not exclude all abstract compact atlases; compact S291 maximum results are not applied on noncompact spaces; graph/bouquet regularization does not solve arbitrary higher-dimensional overlaps; S272 signed/zero intermediate weights and zero-mass rules remain; global-vague uniformity, ordinary weak-net continuity, and fixed-C weak/BL uniformity remain distinct. Literal slopes are integral with rational constants; real PA is their finite scalar real extension with rational spatial walls. The original raw printed-PC envelope has upper-only growth competitors; flooring them by gamma-||u|| gives the same two-sided bounded envelope without assuming raw continuity. R230's supplied completion identifies it with the actual all-continuous-competitor envelope and supplies continuity. That does not prove a global PA approximation domain. The associated P05.2 contact target requires the actual endpoint to enter that domain before an operator/contact integral is evaluated. Neither target is reduced to one obstacle, one cell, a continuous-subcone density statement, or finite-PA contact witnesses. Original P05.1/P05.2 remain OPEN, and candidate=false. None of this is an original balanced counterexample, a classification of all pairs, or a complete contact/operator theorem for arbitrary complexes.
